purpose: Verify 101 independently scoped and individually priced software IP assets. All current source heads and open development records were checked. Three delivered increments and one new prototype have revised estimates; 97 existing prices retain their individual assessments. Website repositories remain excluded digital displays.

verification.browserIntegrity: The public renderer fetches the valuation register and methodology as raw text, recomputes SHA-256 in the browser and compares the result with this attestation.
verification.valuationReconciliation: The public renderer assembles the current asset register, applies published overrides, recalculates asset-level analytical economics and compares aggregate values with the published portfolio totals.
verification.publicSiteDirectory: The public project-site enhancer recomputes the SHA-256 digest of the site directory before presenting its integrity state.
verification.existenceBoundary: The timestamped public publication and matching digests demonstrate existence and integrity of the public commercial record as published. They do not independently prove authorship, legal title, patent priority, source-code identity, scientific validity, security assurance, certified valuation or commercial outcome.
verification.futureEconomicReferences: Verify current asset-level maturity sensitivities using the retained methodology; these are not future asking prices or financial-return forecasts.
verification.sellerReadiness: Verify the dated criteria disclosure and corrected readiness records. Integrity checks establish unchanged published bytes and cross-register consistency; they do not establish completed transfer gates or independent certification.
verification.rightsTransfer: The public renderer verifies the seller-readiness, IP-ownership, software supply-chain, portfolio audit and rights-transfer records. The public transaction layer focuses on the offered rights, third-party obligations and transfer perimeter rather than internal development methods.
verification.projectEvaluations: Each of the 100 active software IP assets has its own identity, evaluation, asking reference and transfer perimeter. The portfolio scope update retains individual evidence and price assessment dates; it does not establish fresh software validation.
verification.projectIdentities: Confirm the 100 unique active TA-IP identifiers, project titles and single feminine reference aliases. Identifiers are stable and may contain gaps. Website/publication repositories are excluded; 12 live digital displays are available.
verification.projectConnections: Verify the proposed-connection register, resolve every member against its independent TA-IP asset record, reject project reuse across combinations and recompute both the combined asking reference and recreation-cost total from the current individual financial references. This verifies identities, unique allocation and arithmetic; it does not establish technical integration.

privacyBoundary: Public records expose seller-side commercial, rights, transfer, evidence and non-sensitive supply-chain metadata only. Internal development methods, proprietary know-how, credentials, customer data, sensitive implementation details and transaction-confidential material remain outside the public showroom.

latestPageRefresh.boundary: All 101 software repositories are accounted for: the 100 existing default branches and 32 open pull requests were checked, and the new OmniFrame source was reviewed. Fresh local checks passed 103 TraceLine tests and 29 SCEP tests. OmniFrame v0.5 passed 37 tests and a development build; its newer v0.7 mandatory syntax gate fails in new test source, so the current full suite and build were not reached and its transfer classification is NOT_READY. TrueLane mandatory validation passed: 95 tests ran, 80 passed and 15 optional PyTorch tests were skipped; no new CUDA or Drive adapter execution is claimed. Changed source, retained validation and unmerged candidates are kept separate. The SCEP checkpoint manifest and tree inventory were reviewed; binary download, restoration and numerical replay were not performed. Prices change only for three implemented main-branch increments and the new OmniFrame prototype. All 97 other existing prices and all 100 existing maturity and readiness classifications are retained. The new OmniFrame prototype has an explicit current-source validation blocker. Website repositories are excluded digital displays. No independent legal, scientific, security or market certification is implied.
